statusDetail: Atomic audit completed across 58/58 catalog checks and five representative paths.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page site with jQuery and Swiper
page.notes: Public Korean gaming news/community portal. Covered homepage, listing, article, community detail and error recovery. Excluded authenticated account, write/post, checkout and destructive flows because they require credentials or commitment.

paths.description: Homepage and primary news-discovery surface; represents global navigation, portal modules, advertising, search and entry content.
News listing archetype; represents category/index browsing and dense repeated story cards.
Editorial article archetype; represents the primary reading journey and rich article metadata.
Community board detail archetype; represents long-form community content and account-adjacent interactions.
Invalid URL recovery path; tests clear HTTP/error recovery and route continuity.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains the same white/red palette as the default screenshot, and the platform probe found no prefers-color-scheme usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint surfaces, text, controls and browser chrome with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, the evaluate probe still found four running animations with 600 ms, 600 ms, 7 s and 20 s durations.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable auto-advance and non-essential animation in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query while preserving essential state changes.

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not implemented and multiple text elements fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; Lighthouse reported contrast ratios as low as 2.09:1 and accessibility score 0.64.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic system colors/forced-color-adjust sparingly, add a prefers-contrast treatment, and raise text/UI contrast to WCAG minimums.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes lack modern transition or attention cues.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition or scroll-state/scroll-timeline implementation; representative screenshots show static chrome and abrupt page-based navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance important route/state changes with View Transitions and add a visible current/scroll-state cue without blocking navigation.

findings.summary: Promotional overlays and dense advertising obscure primary content.
findings.evidence: Homepage, listing and article screenshots show a floating poll/promotion over story content, large house ads, and ad-heavy side rails competing with headlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove load-time overlays, reserve fewer clearly labelled ad slots, and keep promotions inline or user-triggered with a semantic dismissible primitive.

findings.summary: The dismissible promotion uses custom overlay behavior instead of semantic overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: The DOM/evaluate probe found zero dialog, popover and details elements while screenshots show a manually positioned closeable floating promotion.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover for transient promotions or dialog for truly modal flows, with declarative light-dismiss and keyboard behavior.

findings.summary: Mobile rendering is a scaled desktop canvas and user zoom is restricted.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout reported a 1071 CSS-pixel layout viewport/no usable viewport meta and screenshots render three-column desktop layouts as tiny text; Lighthouse flags user-scalable=no.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve one responsive document with width=device-width, initial-scale=1, allow zoom, remove fixed-width shells, and reflow modules at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt at container level.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no @container/container-type usage, while dense cards and side rails remain desktop-proportioned in narrow captures.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce containment and component-level queries for reused story cards, navigation modules and side rails, with intrinsic sizing fallbacks.

findings.summary: Accessible names, contrast, focus and image alternatives are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.64, image-alt and color-contrast failed; the image audit found 96/100 images without alt, and focus probing found several focused controls with no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt (or empty alt for decoration), repair accessible names, meet contrast ratios, and provide consistent :focus-visible indicators.

findings.summary: Primary content is extremely slow to become visible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 13.0 s and Speed Index 20.3 s; the trace measured FCP 8.3 s and LCP 20.6 s. The load transferred 15.8 MB across 378 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, cut initial image/font/third-party bytes, defer below-fold modules, and shorten parser-blocking CSS/script chains.

findings.summary: Resource delivery and shipped code are substantially wasteful.
findings.evidence: HAR found 17 stylesheets, 32 scripts, missing cache headers on key assets and 297 third-party requests; Lighthouse estimates 451 KiB unused JS and 83 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Bundle per template, remove duplicate/unused tags, cache versioned assets, subset fonts, and load analytics/ads only when needed.

findings.summary: Images lack dimensions, responsive sources, lazy loading and modern delivery.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all 100 sampled images missing width/height, 98 legacy-format images, 17 without srcset, and 11 below-fold images not lazy-loaded; HAR includes a 5.3 MB image.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio, generate responsive AVIF/WebP sources, lazy-load below-fold images, and right-size the LCP image with fetchpriority.

findings.summary: The page produces console/network errors and uses brittle legacy platform patterns.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console failed on a 404 script; DOM shows jQuery 1.7.2, javascript: links and onfocus blur patterns, while Lighthouse crawlable-anchors failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove broken resources, replace javascript: anchors and focus suppression with buttons/declarative behavior, and upgrade/remove legacy dependencies.

findings.summary: Some indexing/navigation signals use non-crawlable anchors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO scored 0.83 and crawlable-anchors failed on javascript:void(0) links, including top and menu controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and real href URLs for navigation; preserve crawlable, descriptive links for content destinations.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. All seven cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None; six persist 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark cookies Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: The initial page has a broad tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 24 third-party origins and eight known tracker domains; HAR recorded 297 third-party requests and 15.16 MB classified as third-party-origin traffic.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and remove non-essential trackers, gate optional analytics/ads on consent, batch telemetry, and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.

findings.summary: Search input assistance is deliberately disabled.
findings.evidence: The search form probe reports autocomplete=off and no associated label on the primary search input.
findings.suggestedFix: Give search a persistent accessible label and appropriate autocomplete/search semantics instead of disabling browser assistance.

findings.summary: The page’s asset and third-party budget is disproportionate for a news portal.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 15.8 MB: 11.5 MB images and 2.9 MB fonts, with 378 requests; 301 requests were images and 297 were from origins other than the main origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Set template budgets, right-size images, subset fonts, defer below-fold/media modules, and remove low-value third-party work.
